content.markdown:
# Weld-joint cracking in cold-store conveyor frames

## Verified facts
- AutomVoj reports weld-joint cracking after about 18 months in chilled service, 14 warranty frame replacements this year, no room-temperature reproduction, and a goal to change welding procedure, filler or joint design. [F1]
- Cold-store service is 2–6 °C with suspected combined thermal cycling, condensation and loaded-belt vibration; testing should represent this, not only room-temperature load. [F2]
- AutomVoj lacks low-temperature cyclic-load equipment and know-how; Erić’s group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue machines and a climate chamber to −60 °C. [F3]
- AutomVoj has site photos and measurements of cracked joints and two failed sections in storage. [F4]
- Frames are mild-steel hollow section, MIG/MAG welded and painted for corrosion resistance; specimens should match this production detail. [F5]
- Erić’s chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared, so extended campaigns need advance scheduling. [F6]
- AutomVoj has no dedicated R&D department; technical development happens informally through project work, so a named owner and allocated time are needed. [F7]
- Erić is open to contract research and joint projects on welded-steel fatigue and low-temperature or combined-loading testing; his own low-temperature paper reports a 22% lower fatigue-ductility coefficient at −40 °C, a cold-service risk. [F8]

## Our inference
- Erić’s thermal-cycling and residual-stress work suggests he can separate thermal, mechanical and residual-stress contributions, but his published steels and joint types differ from AutomVoj’s mild-steel hollow-section detail, so transfer must be demonstrated.
- Because AutomVoj cannot reproduce the failure at room temperature, the first factorial should show whether cold, thermal cycling, condensation or vibration dominates; if no single factor repeats the crack, interaction testing is needed.
- The proposal is conditional because Erić’s availability is unknown and equipment is shared, even though his joint-project willingness is open; scheduling confirmation is the main delivery risk.

## Proposed next steps
- Run a first controlled comparison on the two failed sections plus new production-detail coupons (mild-steel hollow section, MIG/MAG crossmember-to-stringer weld, painted condition) using Erić’s servo-hydraulic machine and climate chamber. Proposed baseline: room-temperature load/vibration spectrum from company data. Then change one suspected factor at a time: cold isothermal 2–6 °C; cold plus slow thermal cycling; cold plus condensation; cold plus loaded-belt vibration. Measure crack initiation/growth, stiffness drop and crack-tip observations with FE/ΔK analysis. Go/no-go after two phases: proceed to design variants only if a cold or thermal-cycling condition gives a repeatable crack-driving or life difference versus room-temperature baseline under the company-named service condition; otherwise revise toward condensation/vibration and re-check.
- Test the transfer gap by repeating the comparison on production-representative hollow-section crossmember-to-stringer joints, including paint and condensation, because Erić’s evidence covers other steel grades and butt/cruciform specimens, not this detail at 2–6 °C; compare measured life with his low-temperature and residual-stress models.
- Set negotiation targets: identify at least one dominant factor repeatably across duplicate specimens, rank welding/filler/joint-design variants by measured fatigue life or ΔK under service conditions, and deliver a short report. Proposed 12-month, three-phase plan: specimen extraction and chamber scheduling, first factorial, variant screening; no performance is guaranteed.
- Ask AutomVoj to name an engineering owner and allocate time for specimen supply, service-spectrum data and reviews; ask Erić to reserve chamber/machine slots before campaign start.

## Open questions
- Can Erić confirm availability and scheduling for an extended chamber and servo-hydraulic campaign shared with two other groups?
- Can AutomVoj name a technical owner and allocate engineering time, given there is no dedicated R&D department?
- Can AutomVoj provide loaded-belt vibration spectra, thermal-cycle records and condensation conditions from cold-store sites?
- Should the test coupons include the production paint system and condensation exposure, or is bare-weld testing acceptable for the first comparison?
- Which changes to welding procedure, filler material or crossmember-to-stringer joint design are allowable, and what warranty or cost threshold would define success for AutomVoj?
